items.title: Topic 19: Page Table Structures, TLB & Effective Access Time (EAT)
items.text: Source: Lecture 3.5 (Unit 3) + Textbook Ch. 8 (Silberschatz Ch. 8, Stallings Ch. 7)

items.title: 2-Level (32-bit, 4KB pages)
items.text:
p1 (10 bits) | p2 (10 bits) | d (12 bits)
    │            │           │
    ▼            ▼           ▼
Page Dir    Page Table    Frame

Without TLB: 1 memory access requires 3 physical memory accesses (outer table, inner table, data frame)

items.title: 19.2 Inverted Page Table
items.text:
• One entry per physical frame (not per logical page)
  • Used in 64-bit systems (PowerPC, UltraSPARC)
  • Lookup via hash table (slower than direct indexing)
  • Saves enormous memory for sparse 64-bit address spaces

items.title: Purpose
items.text:
• Hardware cache for page table entries
  • TLB Hit: Translation in TLB → fast (bypass page table)
  • TLB Miss: Walk page table → slow (2+ memory accesses)

items.title: Structure
items.text:
• Associative hardware cache (parallel lookup)
  • Stores recent <VPN, PPN> mappings
  • Typical size: 64-512 entries

items.title: Formula
items.text:
EAT = α × (t_TLB + t_RAM) + (1-α) × (t_TLB + 2 × t_RAM)

Where: - α = TLB hit ratio - t_TLB = TLB lookup time - t_RAM = Main memory access time

items.title: With 2-Level Paging on Miss
items.text:
EAT = α(t_TLB + t_RAM) + (1-α)(t_TLB + 3×t_RAM)
(outer page table + inner page table + data frame)

items.title: 19.5 Key Takeaways
items.text:
1. Multi-level paging = reduces page table memory; 2-level = 3 memory accesses without TLB
  2. Inverted page table = one entry per physical frame; scales with RAM not virtual space
  3. TLB = hardware associative cache for page translations
  4. EAT = α(t_TLB + t_RAM) + (1-α)(t_TLB + k×t_RAM) where k = page table levels + 1

Where: - α = TLB hit ratio - t_TLB = TLB lookup time - t_RAM = Main memory access time

items.title: Topic 20: Virtual Memory — Demand Paging, Page Faults, Copy-on-Write
items.text: Source: Lecture 3.6 (Unit 3) + Textbook Ch. 9 (Silberschatz Ch. 9, Stallings Ch. 8)

items.title: Core Philosophy
items.text:
Pages loaded into physical memory only when referenced (lazy loading)

  • Valid/Invalid bit in PTE:
  • Valid (1) = page in memory
  • Invalid (0) = page on disk or not allocated

items.title: 20.2 Page Fault Handling
items.text:
1. Process accesses invalid page → Page Fault Trap
2. OS checks: Valid access? (within VMA, permissions OK?)
3. Find free frame (or victim via replacement)
4. If victim dirty → Write to swap
5. Read requested page from disk into frame
6. Update PTE (frame #, valid=1)
7. Restart faulting instruction

items.title: 20.3 Minor vs Major Page Fault
items.text: Type Description Latency Minor Page already in RAM (shared library, free list, COW copy) — zero disk I/O Microseconds Major Page must be read from disk Milliseconds

items.title: fork() with COW
items.text:
1. fork() shares all pages read-only (COW)
  2. Parent/child can read freely
  3. On write attempt → Page Fault (protection violation)
  4. OS allocates new frame, copies page, marks read-write
  5. Restarts instruction
// COW example
pid = fork();
// Parent and child share ALL pages (read-only)
// Child calls exec() → new program loaded (no COW needed for that)
// Or child modifies variable → COW triggers → private copy made

items.title: 20.5 Dirty Bit (Modify Bit)
items.text: Value Meaning 0 (Clean) Page not modified → overwrite immediately on replacement 1 (Dirty) Page modified → must write back to disk before replacement (doubles fault time)

items.title: 20.6 Key Takeaways
items.text:
1. Demand Paging = load pages on reference (lazy loading)
  2. Page Fault = trap → check validity → find frame → read from disk → update PTE → restart
  3. Minor Fault = resolves in RAM (COW, shared lib); Major Fault = disk I/O
  4. COW = fork() shares pages read-only; write triggers private copy
  5. Dirty Bit = if 0, no disk write needed on replacement

items.title: 20.7 Exam-Relevant MCQ Patterns
items.text:
• Q84: Demand paging = load pages on reference (lazy loading)
  • Q85: Page fault handling — MMU generates trap to OS first
  • Q86: COW fork — protection violation trap → OS copies page → restarts instruction
  • Q87: Minor vs Major fault — minor = no disk I/O; major = disk read
  • Q88: Dirty bit = if 0, no write-back needed on replacement

items.title: 20.2 Page Fault Handling — Complete Flow
items.text:
CPU executes instruction
        │
        ▼
MMU translates virtual address
        │
        ├──── Valid = 1 ────► Access memory (fast path)
        │
        └──── Valid = 0 ────► PAGE FAULT TRAP
                              │
                              ▼
                     OS Page Fault Handler
                              │
                              ▼
                 ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                 │ 1. Check if valid access:   │
                 │    - Within VMA?            │
                 │    - Correct permissions?   │
                 │    - Stack growth?          │
                 └─────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼ (if invalid → SIGSEGV)
                 ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                 │ 2. Find free frame:         │
                 │    - Free list?             │
                 │    - Page replacement?      │
                 └─────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
                 ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                 │ 3. If victim dirty:         │
                 │    - Write to swap          │
                 │    - Wait for I/O           │
                 └─────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
                 ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                 │ 4. Read requested page:     │
                 │    - From executable?       │
                 │    - From swap?             │
                 │    - Zero-filled?           │
                 └─────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
                 ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                 │ 5. Update PTE:              │
                 │    - Frame #                │
                 │    - Valid = 1              │
                 │    - Ref = 1, Dirty = 0     │
                 └─────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
                    Restart faulting instruction

items.title: 20.3 Minor vs Major Page Faults
items.text:
Aspect Minor Page Fault Major Page Fault Definition Page in RAM but PTE invalid Page must be read from disk Causes COW, shared library, free list, zero page First access, swapped out Disk I/O None Required Latency Microseconds Milliseconds Example fork() COW, shared library text First page access, swapped out 
Minor Fault Flow:
Page Fault → PTE invalid but page in RAM → Update PTE → Restart

Major Fault Flow:
Page Fault → Page on disk → Disk I/O → Update PTE → Restart

items.title: 20.4 Copy-on-Write (COW) — Complete Mechanism
path: Topic 20 (Detailed): Virtual Memory — Demand Paging, Page Faults, Copy-on-Write

items.title: Why COW?
items.text:
Traditional fork():
- Copy ALL pages → Slow, memory-hungry
- Child often exec()s immediately → Waste!

fork() with COW:
- Share pages read-only → Fast, memory-efficient
- On write → Copy only that page
- Child exec()s → No copies needed!
path: Topic 20 (Detailed): Virtual Memory — Demand Paging, Page Faults, Copy-on-Write

items.title: COW Mechanism
items.text:
BEFORE fork():
Parent: Page A (RW) ─┐
                     ├──→ Physical Page A
Parent: Page B (RW) ─┘

AFTER fork() with COW:
Parent: Page A (RO) ─┐
                     ├──→ Physical Page A (shared, ref count=2)
Parent: Page B (RO) ─┘
Child:  Page A (RO) ─┘
Child:  Page B (RO) ─┘

WHEN CHILD WRITES to Page A:
1. Page Fault (protection violation)
2. OS allocates new physical page A'
3. Copies content from A to A'
4. Updates child's PTE: Frame=A', RW, Valid=1
5. Decrements ref count of A
6. Restarts instruction

AFTER COW:
Parent: Page A (RW) → Physical Page A
Child:  Page A (RW) → Physical Page A'
path: Topic 20 (Detailed): Virtual Memory — Demand Paging, Page Faults, Copy-on-Write

items.title: COW Implementation Details
items.text:
// Simplified kernel COW logic
void handle_cow_fault(vaddr_t vaddr) {
    pte_t *pte = get_pte(current->mm, vaddr);

    if (!pte_present(pte)) {
        // Major fault - handle normally
        do_page_fault(vaddr);
        return;
    }

    // Check if COW page
    if (pte_cow(pte)) {
        // Allocate new page
        page_t *new_page = alloc_page();
        if (!new_page) OOM();

        // Copy content
        copy_page(new_page, pte_page(pte));

        // Update PTE
        pte_clear_cow(pte);
        pte_set_page(pte, new_page);
        pte_set_writable(pte);
        pte_set_dirty(pte);

        // Decrement ref count of old page
        dec_page_ref(pte_page(pte));

        // Flush TLB
        flush_tlb(vaddr);

        return; // Restart instruction
    }

    // Not COW - regular protection fault
    do_sigsegv(vaddr);
}

items.title: COW Example: fork() + exec()
items.text:
// Parent
pid = fork();

if (pid == 0) {
    // Child
    // All pages shared COW
    // If child calls exec():
    //   - New address space created
    //   - Old COW pages discarded
    //   - NO copies made!
    execl("/bin/ls", "ls", NULL);
} else {
    // Parent continues
    wait(NULL);
}

Without COW: fork() copies all pages → exec() throws them away → HUGE waste! With COW: fork() shares pages → exec() discards references → ZERO waste!

items.title: Impact on Page Fault Time
items.text:
Clean page replacement:
1. Select victim
2. Overwrite frame with new page
3. Update PTE
Time: ~100ns (memory only)

Dirty page replacement:
1. Select victim
2. Write victim to swap (disk I/O)
3. Wait for I/O completion
4. Overwrite frame with new page
5. Update PTE
Time: ~10ms (100,000x slower!)

items.title: 20.6 Complete Demand Paging Simulator
items.text:
/*
 * File: demand_paging.c
 * Simulates demand paging with page fault handling
 * Compile: gcc -o demand_paging demand_paging.c
 */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>

#define PAGE_SIZE 4096
#define VIRTUAL_PAGES 64
#define PHYSICAL_FRAMES 16
#define SWAP_SLOTS 64

typedef enum { INVALID, IN_MEMORY, ON_DISK } page_state_t;

typedef struct {
    int frame;          // Physical frame # (if IN_MEMORY)
    int disk_block;     // Swap slot (if ON_DISK)
    page_state_t state;
    int ref_bit;        // Reference bit
    int dirty_bit;      // Dirty bit
    int prot;           // Protection bits
    int last_access;    // For LRU
} PTE;

typedef struct {
    int pid;
    int page;
    int frame;
    int dirty;
} FrameInfo;

PTE page_table[VIRTUAL_PAGES];
FrameInfo frames[PHYSICAL_FRAMES];
int free_frames[PHYSICAL_FRAMES];
int free_count;
int swap_map[SWAP_SLOTS];  // Which (pid, page) in each swap slot
int time_counter = 0;

void init_system() {
    for (int i = 0; i < VIRTUAL_PAGES; i++) {
        page_table[i].state = INVALID;
        page_table[i].frame = -1;
        page_table[i].disk_block = -1;
        page_table[i].ref_bit = 0;
        page_table[i].dirty_bit = 0;
        page_table[i].prot = 0x7; // RWX
    }

    for (int i = 0; i < PHYSICAL_FRAMES; i++) {
        frames[i].pid = -1;
        frames[i].page = -1;
        frames[i].frame = i;
        frames[i].dirty = 0;
        free_frames[i] = i;
    }
    free_count = PHYSICAL_FRAMES;

    for (int i = 0; i < SWAP_SLOTS; i++) {
        swap_map[i] = -1;
    }
}

int allocate_frame() {
    if (free_count > 0) {
        return free_frames[--free_count];
    }
    return -1; // Need page replacement
}

int allocate_swap_slot() {
    for (int i = 0; i < SWAP_SLOTS; i++) {
        if (swap_map[i] == -1) {
            swap_map[i] = 1; // Mark occupied
            return i;
        }
    }
    return -1; // Swap full
}

void free_swap_slot(int slot) {
    if (slot >= 0 && slot < SWAP_SLOTS) {
        swap_map[slot] = -1;
    }
}

void simulate_disk_write(int frame) {
    // Simulate disk I/O latency
    printf("    [DISK WRITE] Frame %d to swap\n", frame);
}

void simulate_disk_read(int swap_slot, int frame) {
    // Simulate disk I/O latency
    printf("    [DISK READ] Swap slot %d to frame %d\n", swap_slot, frame);
}

int select_victim_lru() {
    int oldest = -1;
    int victim = -1;
    for (int i = 0; i < PHYSICAL_FRAMES; i++) {
        if (frames[i].pid != -1) {
            // In real system, would check page_table[pid][page].last_access
            // Simplified: pick first dirty frame, else first frame
        }
    }
    // Simplified: return first frame (FIFO-like)
    for (int i = 0; i < PHYSICAL_FRAMES; i++) {
        if (frames[i].pid != -1) return i;
    }
    return 0;
}

void handle_page_fault(int pid, int vpage, int is_write) {
    printf("\n[PAGE FAULT] PID=%d, Virtual Page=%d, Write=%d\n", pid, vpage, is_write);
    time_counter++;

    PTE *pte = &page_table[vpage];

    // Check if valid access (simplified)
    if (pte->state == INVALID) {
        // First access - allocate zero-filled page
        printf("  First access to page %d\n", vpage);

        int frame = allocate_frame();
        if (frame == -1) {
            // Need page replacement
            int victim = select_victim_lru();
            FrameInfo *victim_info = &frames[victim];

            if (victim_info->dirty) {
                // Write to swap
                int swap_slot = allocate_swap_slot();
                simulate_disk_write(victim_info->frame);
                victim_info->dirty = 0;

                // Update victim's PTE
                // In real system, would find victim's PTE and update
            }

            // Use victim's frame
            frames[victim].pid = pid;
            frames[victim].page = vpage;
            frames[victim].dirty = is_write;

            pte->frame = victim;
            pte->state = IN_MEMORY;
            pte->ref_bit = 1;
            pte->dirty_bit = is_write;

            printf("  Replaced frame %d, loaded page %d\n", victim, vpage);
        } else {
            // Zero-filled page
            frames[frame].pid = pid;
            frames[frame].page = vpage;
            frames[frame].dirty = is_write;

            pte->frame = frame;
            pte->state = IN_MEMORY;
            pte->ref_bit = 1;
            pte->dirty_bit = is_write;

            printf("  Allocated new frame %d for page %d\n", frame, vpage);
        }
    } else if (pte->state == ON_DISK) {
        // Major page fault - read from swap
        printf("  Major fault: Page on disk\n");

        int frame = allocate_frame();
        if (frame == -1) {
            // Page replacement needed (same as above)
            int victim = select_victim_lru();
            frames[victim].pid = pid;
            frames[victim].page = vpage;
            frames[victim].dirty = is_write;
            pte->frame = victim;
            pte->state = IN_MEMORY;
            pte->ref_bit = 1;
            pte->dirty_bit = is_write;
            simulate_disk_read(pte->disk_block, victim);
        } else {
            frames[frame].pid = pid;
            frames[frame].page = vpage;
            frames[frame].dirty = is_write;
            pte->frame = frame;
            pte->state = IN_MEMORY;
            pte->ref_bit = 1;
            pte->dirty_bit = is_write;
            simulate_disk_read(pte->disk_block, frame);
        }
    }

    // Clear disk block since now in memory
    pte->disk_block = -1;
}

void access_memory(int pid, int vpage, int is_write) {
    if (vpage < 0 || vpage >= VIRTUAL_PAGES) {
        printf("Invalid page %d\n", vpage);
        return;
    }

    PTE *pte = &page_table[vpage];

    if (pte->state == IN_MEMORY && pte->frame >= 0) {
        // HIT
        if (is_write) {
            page_table[vpage].dirty_bit = 1;
            frames[pte->frame].dirty = 1;
        }
        page_table[vpage].ref_bit = 1;
        page_table[vpage].last_access = time_counter++;
        printf("Hit: PID=%d, Page=%d, Frame=%d, Write=%d\n", 
               pid, vpage, pte->frame, is_write);
    } else {
        // PAGE FAULT
        handle_page_fault(pid, vpage, is_write);
    }
}

void print_stats() {
    int in_mem = 0, on_disk = 0, invalid = 0;
    int dirty = 0;

    for (int i = 0; i < VIRTUAL_PAGES; i++) {
        switch (page_table[i].state) {
            case IN_MEMORY: in_mem++; if (page_table[i].dirty_bit) dirty++; break;
            case ON_DISK: on_disk++; break;
            case INVALID: invalid++; break;
        }
    }

    printf("\n=== Memory Stats ===\n");
    printf("In memory: %d, On disk: %d, Invalid: %d\n", in_mem, on_disk, invalid);
    printf("Dirty pages: %d\n", dirty);
    printf("Free frames: %d\n", free_count);
}

int main() {
    init_system();

    // Simulate process accessing memory
    printf("=== Demand Paging Simulation ===\n");

    // Process 0 accesses pages 0,1,2,3 (first time)
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
        access_memory(0, i, 0); // Read
    }

    // Process 0 writes to page 1
    access_memory(0, 1, 1);

    // Process 0 accesses page 0 again (hit)
    access_memory(0, 0, 0);

    // Fill up memory
    for (int i = 4; i < 20; i++) {
        access_memory(0, i, 0);
    }

    print_stats();

    return 0;
}

2-Level (32-bit, 4KB):

Entries = 2^20 = 1,048,576

items.title: 20.8 TLB (Translation Lookaside Buffer)
path: Topic 20 (Detailed): Virtual Memory — Demand Paging, Page Faults, Copy-on-Write

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Hardware cache for page table entries.
path: Topic 20 (Detailed): Virtual Memory — Demand Paging, Page Faults, Copy-on-Write

items.title: TLB Hit/Miss
items.text:
TLB Hit:  VPN → TLB → PPN → Physical Address (fast)
TLB Miss: VPN → TLB (miss) → Page Table Walk → PPN → Update TLB → Physical Address
path: Topic 20 (Detailed): Virtual Memory — Demand Paging, Page Faults, Copy-on-Write

items.title: Effective Access Time (EAT)
items.text:
EAT = α × (t_TLB + t_RAM) + (1-α) × (t_TLB + k × t_RAM)

Where:
α = TLB hit ratio
t_TLB = TLB lookup time
t_RAM = Main memory access time
k = page table levels + 1 (data access)
path: Topic 20 (Detailed): Virtual Memory — Demand Paging, Page Faults, Copy-on-Write

items.title: Example Calculation
items.text:
Given:
TLB hit ratio (α) = 80% = 0.80
TLB access time = 20 ns
Memory access time = 100 ns
Single-level paging (k=2 on miss)

EAT = 0.80 × (20 + 100) + 0.20 × (20 + 2×100)
    = 0.80 × 120 + 0.20 × 220
    = 96 + 44 = 140 ns
path: Topic 20 (Detailed): Virtual Memory — Demand Paging, Page Faults, Copy-on-Write

items.title: Two-Level Paging EAT
items.text:
Without TLB: 3 memory accesses (outer table + inner table + data)
With TLB miss on 2-level: TLB + 3×RAM

EAT = α(t_TLB + t_RAM) + (1-α)(t_TLB + 3×t_RAM)

items.title: 20.9 Inverted Page Table
path: Topic 20 (Detailed): Virtual Memory — Demand Paging, Page Faults, Copy-on-Write

items.text:

  • Size scales with physical RAM, not virtual space

items.title: 21.1 Page Replacement Problem
items.text:
When a page fault occurs and no free frames exist, OS must choose a victim frame to evict.

Page Fault → No free frames → Choose victim → Write if dirty → Read new page → Update PTE → Restart

Goal: Minimize page faults.

Let me redo with proper timestamps:

items.text:
• Circular list of frames with reference bit (R)
  • Hand sweeps around:
  • If R=0 → victim (replace)
  • If R=1 → R=0, give second chance, advance hand

items.title: 4 Priority Classes (Best → Worst)
items.text: Priority (Ref, Dirty) Reason 1 (Best) (0, 0) Not referenced, clean → no write-back 2 (0, 1) Not referenced, dirty → needs write-back 3 (1, 0) Referenced, clean → recently used 4 (Worst) (1, 1) Referenced and dirty
path: Topic 21 (Detailed): Page Replacement — Complete Traces, Belady's Anomaly, Clock Algorithm

items.title: Algorithm
items.text:
1. Scan for (0,0) — if found, replace
  2. If not found, scan for (0,1) — clear ref, advance
  3. If not found, scan for (1,0) — clear ref, advance
  4. If not found, scan for (1,1) — clear ref, advance
  5. Repeat from step 1

Linux uses variant of enhanced clock.

items.title: 21.7 Complete Page Replacement Simulator
items.text:
/*
 * File: page_replacement.c
 * Complete simulator for FIFO, OPT, LRU, Clock, Enhanced Clock
 * Compile: gcc -o page_replacement page_replacement.c
 */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <limits.h>

#define MAX_FRAMES 10
#define MAX_REFS 100

typedef struct {
    int page;
    int ref_bit;
    int dirty_bit;
    int timestamp;  // For LRU
    int loaded_time; // For FIFO
} Frame;

int refs[] = {1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
int n_refs = 12;

void print_frames(Frame frames[], int n, int time) {
    printf("  [");
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (frames[i].page == -1) printf(" - ");
        else printf(" %d(R=%d,D=%d) ", frames[i].page, frames[i].ref_bit, frames[i].dirty_bit);
    }
    printf("]\n");
}

/* FIFO */
int fifo(int frames_count) {
    Frame frames[MAX_FRAMES];
    for (int i = 0; i < frames_count; i++) frames[i].page = -1;

    int victim = 0;
    int faults = 0;
    int time = 0;

    printf("\n=== FIFO (%d frames) ===\n", frames_count);

    for (int i = 0; i < n_refs; i++) {
        int page = refs[i];
        bool hit = false;

        for (int j = 0; j < frames_count; j++) {
            if (frames[j].page == page) { hit = true; break; }
        }

        if (!hit) {
            faults++;
            frames[victim].page = page;
            frames[victim].loaded_time = time++;
            victim = (victim + 1) % frames_count;
            printf("Ref %d: Fault  ", page);
        } else {
            printf("Ref %d: Hit    ", page);
        }
        print_frames(frames, frames_count, time);
    }
    printf("Total faults: %d\n", faults);
    return faults;
}

/* OPT - Optimal */
int opt(int frames_count) {
    Frame frames[MAX_FRAMES];
    for (int i = 0; i < frames_count; i++) frames[i].page = -1;

    int faults = 0;

    printf("\n=== OPTIMAL (%d frames) ===\n", frames_count);

    for (int i = 0; i < n_refs; i++) {
        int page = refs[i];
        bool hit = false;

        for (int j = 0; j < frames_count; j++) {
            if (frames[j].page == page) { hit = true; break; }
        }

        if (!hit) {
            faults++;
            // Find free frame
            int free_idx = -1;
            for (int j = 0; j < frames_count; j++) {
                if (frames[j].page == -1) { free_idx = j; break; }
            }

            if (free_idx != -1) {
                frames[free_idx].page = page;
            } else {
                // Find page used farthest in future
                int victim = -1;
                int farthest = -1;

                for (int j = 0; j < frames_count; j++) {
                    int next_use = INT_MAX;
                    for (int k = i + 1; k < n_refs; k++) {
                        if (refs[k] == frames[j].page) {
                            next_use = k;
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                    if (next_use > farthest) {
                        farthest = next_use;
                        victim = j;
                    }
                }
                frames[victim].page = page;
            }
            printf("Ref %d: Fault  ", page);
        } else {
            printf("Ref %d: Hit    ", page);
        }
        print_frames(frames, frames_count, i);
    }
    printf("Total faults: %d\n", faults);
    return faults;
}

/* LRU */
int lru(int frames_count) {
    Frame frames[MAX_FRAMES];
    for (int i = 0; i < frames_count; i++) frames[i].page = -1;

    int faults = 0;
    int time = 0;

    printf("\n=== LRU (%d frames) ===\n", frames_count);

    for (int i = 0; i < n_refs; i++) {
        int page = refs[i];
        bool hit = false;
        int hit_idx = -1;

        for (int j = 0; j < frames_count; j++) {
            if (frames[j].page == page) { hit = true; hit_idx = j; break; }
        }

        if (!hit) {
            faults++;
            // Find free frame
            int free_idx = -1;
            for (int j = 0; j < frames_count; j++) {
                if (frames[j].page == -1) { free_idx = j; break; }
            }

            if (free_idx != -1) {
                frames[free_idx].page = page;
                frames[free_idx].timestamp = time++;
            } else {
                // Find LRU (oldest timestamp)
                int victim = 0;
                int oldest = frames[0].timestamp;
                for (int j = 1; j < frames_count; j++) {
                    if (frames[j].timestamp < oldest) {
                        oldest = frames[j].timestamp;
                        victim = j;
                    }
                }
                frames[victim].page = page;
                frames[victim].timestamp = time++;
            }
            printf("Ref %d: Fault  ", page);
        } else {
            frames[hit_idx].timestamp = time++;
            printf("Ref %d: Hit    ", page);
        }
        print_frames(frames, frames_count, time);
    }
    printf("Total faults: %d\n", faults);
    return faults;
}

/* Clock (Second-Chance) */
int clock_algo(int frames_count) {
    Frame frames[MAX_FRAMES];
    for (int i = 0; i < frames_count; i++) {
        frames[i].page = -1;
        frames[i].ref_bit = 0;
    }

    int faults = 0;
    int hand = 0;

    printf("\n=== CLOCK (%d frames) ===\n", frames_count);

    for (int i = 0; i < n_refs; i++) {
        int page = refs[i];
        bool hit = false;
        int hit_idx = -1;

        for (int j = 0; j < frames_count; j++) {
            if (frames[j].page == page) { hit = true; hit_idx = j; break; }
        }

        if (!hit) {
            faults++;
            // Find free frame
            int free_idx = -1;
            for (int j = 0; j < frames_count; j++) {
                if (frames[j].page == -1) { free_idx = j; break; }
            }

            if (free_idx != -1) {
                frames[free_idx].page = page;
                frames[free_idx].ref_bit = 1;
            } else {
                // Clock sweep
                while (true) {
                    if (frames[hand].ref_bit == 0) {
                        // Victim found
                        frames[hand].page = page;
                        frames[hand].ref_bit = 1;
                        hand = (hand + 1) % frames_count;
                        break;
                    } else {
                        // Second chance
                        frames[hand].ref_bit = 0;
                        hand = (hand + 1) % frames_count;
                    }
                }
            }
            printf("Ref %d: Fault  ", page);
        } else {
            frames[hit_idx].ref_bit = 1;
            printf("Ref %d: Hit    ", page);
        }
        print_frames(frames, frames_count, i);
    }
    printf("Total faults: %d\n", faults);
    return faults;
}

/* Enhanced Clock */
int enhanced_clock(int frames_count) {
    Frame frames[MAX_FRAMES];
    for (int i = 0; i < frames_count; i++) {
        frames[i].page = -1;
        frames[i].ref_bit = 0;
        frames[i].dirty_bit = 0;
    }

    int faults = 0;
    int hand = 0;

    printf("\n=== ENHANCED CLOCK (%d frames) ===\n", frames_count);

    for (int i = 0; i < n_refs; i++) {
        int page = refs[i];
        bool hit = false;
        int hit_idx = -1;

        for (int j = 0; j < frames_count; j++) {
            if (frames[j].page == page) { hit = true; hit_idx = j; break; }
        }

        if (!hit) {
            faults++;
            // Find free frame
            int free_idx = -1;
            for (int j = 0; j < frames_count; j++) {
                if (frames[j].page == -1) { free_idx = j; break; }
            }

            if (free_idx != -1) {
                frames[free_idx].page = page;
                frames[free_idx].ref_bit = 1;
                frames[free_idx].dirty_bit = 0;
            } else {
                // Enhanced clock: 4 passes
                for (int pass = 0; pass < 4; pass++) {
                    int start_hand = hand;
                    bool found = false;

                    do {
                        int r = frames[hand].ref_bit;
                        int d = frames[hand].dirty_bit;

                        // Priority: (0,0) > (0,1) > (1,0) > (1,1)
                        bool match = false;
                        if (pass == 0 && r == 0 && d == 0) match = true;
                        else if (pass == 1 && r == 0 && d == 1) match = true;
                        else if (pass == 2 && r == 1 && d == 0) match = true;
                        else if (pass == 3 && r == 1 && d == 1) match = true;

                        if (match) {
                            frames[hand].page = page;
                            frames[hand].ref_bit = 1;
                            frames[hand].dirty_bit = 0;
                            hand = (hand + 1) % frames_count;
                            found = true;
                            break;
                        } else {
                            // Clear ref bit, advance
                            frames[hand].ref_bit = 0;
                            hand = (hand + 1) % frames_count;
                        }
                    } while (hand != start_hand);

                    if (found) break;
                }
            }
            printf("Ref %d: Fault  ", page);
        } else {
            frames[hit_idx].ref_bit = 1;
            frames[hit_idx].dirty_bit = 1;  // Simulate write
            printf("Ref %d: Hit    ", page);
        }
        print_frames(frames, frames_count, i);
    }
    printf("Total faults: %d\n", faults);
    return faults;
}

int main() {
    // Test with 3 frames and 4 frames to show Belady's Anomaly
    printf("Reference String: ");
    for (int i = 0; i < n_refs; i++) printf("%d ", refs[i]);
    printf("\n");

    // 3 frames
    fifo(3);
    opt(3);
    lru(3);
    clock_algo(3);
    enhanced_clock(3);

    printf("\n\n=== BELADY'S ANOMALY DEMO ===\n");
    printf("FIFO 3 frames: ");
    fifo(3);
    printf("FIFO 4 frames: ");
    fifo(4);
    printf("LRU 3 frames:  ");
    lru(3);
    printf("LRU 4 frames:  ");
    lru(4);
    printf("OPT 3 frames:  ");
    opt(3);
    printf("OPT 4 frames:  ");
    opt(4);

    return 0;
}

Output shows: 

FIFO 3 frames: 9 faults
FIFO 4 frames: 10 faults  ← BELADY'S ANOMALY!
LRU 3 frames:  10 faults
LRU 4 frames:  8 faults   ← No anomaly!
OPT 3 frames:  7 faults
OPT 4 frames:  6 faults   ← No anomaly!

items.text: Increasing frame allocation → page faults increase - Example string: 1,2,3,4,1,2,5,1,2,3,4,5 - 3 frames = 9 faults, 4 frames = 10 faults

items.title: Stack Algorithms (LRU & Optimal)
items.text: The set of pages in memory for n frames is always a subset of pages for n+1 frames. → LRU and Optimal NEVER suffer from Belady's Anomaly

items.title: 21.7 Key Takeaways
items.text:
1. FIFO = Belady's Anomaly YES; LRU/OPT = Belady's Anomaly NO (stack algorithms)
  2. Clock/Second-Chance = circular queue + reference bit; approximates LRU
  3. Enhanced Clock = (ref, dirty) priority: (0,0) > (0,1) > (1,0) > (1,1)
  4. Frame Allocation: Equal, Proportional, Priority, Working Set
  5. Thrashing = Σ WSSᵢ > D; detected by high paging + low CPU
  6. Working Set = pages referenced in last Δ time; based on locality
  7. PFF = upper/lower fault rate bounds → dynamic frame adjustment
  8. Global replacement = thrashing contagion risk; Local = isolates

items.title: 22.1 NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access) Architecture
path: Topic 22 (Detailed): NUMA, Memory Locality & Enhanced Clock Replacement

items.title: The Problem: UMA Doesn't Scale
items.text:
UMA (Uniform Memory Access):
        CPU 0          CPU 1          CPU 2          CPU 3
          │              │              │              │
          └──────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────┘
                         ▼
              ┌───────────────────┐
              │   SHARED MEMORY   │  (Single bus, uniform latency)
              └───────────────────┘

Problem: Bus contention → latency increases with CPU count
path: Topic 22 (Detailed): NUMA, Memory Locality & Enhanced Clock Replacement

items.title: NUMA Solution
items.text:
NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access):
         NODE 0                          NODE 1
    ┌──────────────────┐           ┌──────────────────┐
    │  CPU 0  CPU 1    │           │  CPU 2  CPU 3    │
    │       │          │           │       │          │
    │  ┌────┴────┐     │           │  ┌────┴────┐     │
    │  │ LOCAL   │     │  INTERCONNECT  │ LOCAL   │     │
    │  │  MEM    │     │                │  MEM    │     │
    │  └─────────┘     │                └─────────┘     │
    └──────────────────┘           └──────────────────┘

Local access:  ~100ns (direct on node's bus)
Remote access: ~200-400ns (traverse interconnect)

items.text: Aspect UMA NUMA Memory latency Uniform Varies by CPU-memory distance Scalability Limited (~8-16 CPUs) High (64+ CPUs) Programming model Simple Requires NUMA awareness OS support Standard NUMA-aware scheduler/allocator

items.title: 22.2 Memory Locality & First-Touch Policy
path: Topic 22 (Detailed): NUMA, Memory Locality & Enhanced Clock Replacement

items.title: First-Touch Policy
items.text:
When a page is first WRITTEN (not just allocated):
1. OS allocates physical frame on the CURRENT NODE
2. Page stays on that node unless migrated

Example:
Process on Node 0 calls malloc(100MB)
  → Pages marked "not present"
Process writes to page 0 on Node 0
  → Page fault → allocated on Node 0
Process migrates to Node 1, writes to page 1
  → Page fault → allocated on Node 1
path: Topic 22 (Detailed): NUMA, Memory Locality & Enhanced Clock Replacement

items.title: Code Example: First-Touch Matters
items.text:
// BAD: All memory allocated on master thread's node
double *array = malloc(N * sizeof(double));
#pragma omp parallel for
for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
    array[i] = 0.0;  // All pages allocated on master's node!
}

// GOOD: Each thread touches its own pages
double *array = malloc(N * sizeof(double));
#pragma omp parallel for
for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
    array[i] = 0.0;  // Each thread's pages allocated on its node
}

items.title: 22.3 NUMA-Aware Scheduler
path: Topic 22 (Detailed): NUMA, Memory Locality & Enhanced Clock Replacement

items.title: Goals
items.text:
1. Prefer local memory — Keep processes on nodes where their memory resides
  2. Balance load — Don't overload one node while others idle
  3. Minimize migrations — Moving processes is expensive (cache cold, remote memory)
path: Topic 22 (Detailed): NUMA, Memory Locality & Enhanced Clock Replacement

items.title: Scheduler Policies
items.text:
Linux CFS NUMA Balancing:
1. Task NUMA group tracking
   - Track which nodes a task's memory is on
   - Periodic NUMA hinting faults to detect access patterns

2. Load balancing with NUMA cost
   - Calculate "imbalance" including remote memory penalty
   - Prefer same-node migration
   - Cross-node only for severe imbalance

3. Wake-up affinity
   - Wake task on same node as waker (shared data likely)
   - Or on node where task's memory resides

items.title: 22.4 Clock Page Replacement — Complete Implementation

items.title: Basic Clock (Second-Chance)
items.text:
Data Structure:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Circular list of frames with reference bit (R)    │
│                                                     │
│  Frame 0: Page 5, R=1  ← hand                      │
│  Frame 1: Page 2, R=0                               │
│  Frame 2: Page 7, R=1                               │
│  Frame 3: Page 1, R=0                               │
│  Frame 4: Page 9, R=1                               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Algorithm:
1. Hand points to next frame to examine
2. If R=0 → VICTIM (replace)
3. If R=1 → R=0 (second chance), advance hand
4. Repeat until victim found

items.title: 22.5 Enhanced Clock (With Dirty Bit)
path: Topic 22 (Detailed): NUMA, Memory Locality & Enhanced Clock Replacement

items.title: 4 Priority Classes
items.text: Priority (Ref, Dirty) Name Action 1 (Best) (0, 0) Clean, unreferenced Replace immediately (no I/O) 2 (0, 1) Dirty, unreferenced Write to disk, then replace 3 (1, 0) Referenced, clean Clear R, give second chance 4 (Worst) (1, 1) Referenced, dirty Clear R, give second chance
path: Topic 22 (Detailed): NUMA, Memory Locality & Enhanced Clock Replacement

items.title: Multi-Pass Algorithm
items.text:
Pass 1: Scan for (0,0) — replace immediately if found
Pass 2: Scan for (0,1) — clear R, advance; if completes → write dirty, replace
Pass 3: Scan for (1,0) — clear R, advance
Pass 4: Scan for (1,1) — clear R, advance
Repeat from Pass 1
path: Topic 22 (Detailed): NUMA, Memory Locality & Enhanced Clock Replacement

items.title: Why (0,0) First?
items.text:
• No disk write needed → fastest replacement
  • Clean page → can be overwritten immediately
  • Unreferenced → unlikely to be needed soon
path: Topic 22 (Detailed): NUMA, Memory Locality & Enhanced Clock Replacement

items.title: Why (1,1) Last?
items.text:
• Recently used → likely to be used again
  • Modified → requires disk write before replacement
  • Maximum cost to replace

items.title: 22.6 Complete Enhanced Clock Implementation
items.text:
/*
 * File: enhanced_clock.c
 * Complete Enhanced Clock with 4-pass algorithm
 * Compile: gcc -o enhanced_clock enhanced_clock.c
 */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

#define MAX_FRAMES 10

typedef struct {
    int page;        // Page number (-1 = empty)
    int ref_bit;     // Reference bit (R)
    int dirty_bit;   // Dirty bit (D)
} Frame;

Frame frames[MAX_FRAMES];
int n_frames;
int hand = 0;

// Priority: (R,D) pairs in order of preference
// Pass 0: (0,0) - best
// Pass 1: (0,1)
// Pass 2: (1,0)
// Pass 3: (1,1) - worst

int find_victim() {
    for (int pass = 0; pass < 4; pass++) {
        int start_hand = hand;
        bool found = false;

        do {
            int r = frames[hand].ref_bit;
            int d = frames[hand].dirty_bit;
            bool match = false;

            // Check if this frame matches current pass priority
            if (pass == 0 && r == 0 && d == 0) match = true;
            else if (pass == 1 && r == 0 && d == 1) match = true;
            else if (pass == 2 && r == 1 && d == 0) match = true;
            else if (pass == 3 && r == 1 && d == 1) match = true;

            if (match) {
                // Victim found!
                int victim = hand;
                hand = (hand + 1) % n_frames;
                return victim;
            } else {
                // Not a match - clear reference bit, advance hand
                frames[hand].ref_bit = 0;
                hand = (hand + 1) % n_frames;
            }
        } while (hand != start_hand);
    }

    // Should never reach here (pass 3 always matches)
    int victim = hand;
    hand = (hand + 1) % n_frames;
    return victim;
}

void access_page(int page, int is_write) {
    // Check if page already in memory
    for (int i = 0; i < n_frames; i++) {
        if (frames[i].page == page) {
            // HIT
            frames[i].ref_bit = 1;
            if (is_write) frames[i].dirty_bit = 1;
            printf("Hit: Page %d (R=%d, D=%d)\n", page, frames[i].ref_bit, frames[i].dirty_bit);
            return;
        }
    }

    // PAGE FAULT
    printf("Fault: Page %d\n", page);

    // Find free frame
    for (int i = 0; i < n_frames; i++) {
        if (frames[i].page == -1) {
            frames[i].page = page;
            frames[i].ref_bit = 1;
            frames[i].dirty_bit = is_write ? 1 : 0;
            printf("  Loaded into free frame %d (R=%d, D=%d)\n", i, frames[i].ref_bit, frames[i].dirty_bit);
            return;
        }
    }

    // Need replacement - use enhanced clock
    int victim = find_victim();

    if (frames[victim].dirty_bit) {
        printf("  [DISK WRITE] Frame %d (page %d) was dirty\n", victim, frames[victim].page);
    }

    frames[victim].page = page;
    frames[victim].ref_bit = 1;
    frames[victim].dirty_bit = is_write ? 1 : 0;
    printf("  Replaced frame %d with page %d (R=%d, D=%d)\n", victim, page, frames[victim].ref_bit, frames[victim].dirty_bit);
}

void print_frames() {
    printf("Frames: ");
    for (int i = 0; i < n_frames; i++) {
        if (frames[i].page == -1) printf("[empty] ");
        else printf("[P%d R%d D%d] ", frames[i].page, frames[i].ref_bit, frames[i].dirty_bit);
    }
    printf("  (hand=%d)\n", hand);
}

int main() {
    // Reference string from slides
    int refs[] = {1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    int n_refs = 12;

    n_frames = 3;
    for (int i = 0; i < n_frames; i++) frames[i].page = -1;

    printf("=== Enhanced Clock (3 frames) ===\n");
    printf("Reference string: ");
    for (int i = 0; i < n_refs; i++) printf("%d ", refs[i]);
    printf("\n\n");

    for (int i = 0; i < n_refs; i++) {
        access_page(refs[i], 0); // All reads for simplicity
        print_frames();
    }

    return 0;
}

items.title: Challenge: Page Replacement Across NUMA Nodes
items.text:
Problem:
- Page replacement chooses victim globally
- Victim might be on remote node
- Evicting remote page = remote disk I/O (slow)
- Allocating replacement page on local node = good

Solution: NUMA-aware page replacement
1. Prefer local victims
2. If no local victim, consider remote with penalty
3. Allocate replacement on requesting node

items.title: Migrate-on-Fault
items.text:
When process on Node 0 accesses page on Node 1:
1. Page fault (page present but remote)
2. Option A: Migrate page to Node 0
   - Allocate local frame
   - Copy content
   - Update PTE
   - Free remote frame
3. Option B: Keep remote, track NUMA hint
   - Increment NUMA fault counter
   - If threshold exceeded → migrate

items.title: Topic 22: NUMA, Memory Locality & Clock Page Replacement
items.text: Source: Lecture 3.8 (Unit 3) + Textbook Ch. 9 (Silberschatz Ch. 9)

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
• Memory access latency varies by CPU-memory distance
  • Each CPU has "local" memory (fast) and "remote" memory (slow)
  • Multiple nodes: each with CPUs + local RAM, connected via interconnect

items.title: Memory Locality
items.text: Access Type Latency Local ~100ns (direct on CPU's local bus) Remote ~200-400ns (traverse interconnect)

items.title: First-Touch Policy
items.text:
• Page allocated on node where first touched
  • OS tries to allocate on same node as accessing thread

items.title: OS Scheduler Support
items.text:
• Prefers same-node migration
  • Cross-node only for severe imbalance
  • Tracks NUMA topology

items.title: Basic Algorithm
items.text:
• Circular list of frames with reference bit
  • Hand sweeps around:
  • If ref=0 → victim (replace)
  • If ref=1 → ref=0, give second chance, advance hand
Frame:  [P1,1] [P2,0] [P3,1] [P4,1] [P5,0]
              ↑ hand

items.title: Logic
items.text:
while (true):
    if frame[hand].ref == 0:
        victim = hand
        break
    else:
        frame[hand].ref = 0  // second chance
        hand = (hand + 1) % N

items.title: 4 Priority Classes (Best → Worst)
items.text: Priority (Ref, Dirty) Reason 1 (Best) (0, 0) Not referenced, clean → no write-back 2 (0, 1) Not referenced, dirty → needs write-back 3 (1, 0) Referenced, clean → recently used 4 (Worst) (1, 1) Referenced and dirty

items.title: Algorithm
items.text:
1. Scan for (0,0) — if found, replace
  2. If not found, scan for (0,1) — clear ref, advance
  3. If not found, scan for (1,0) — clear ref, advance
  4. If not found, scan for (1,1) — clear ref, advance
  5. Repeat from step 1

Linux uses variant of enhanced clock.

items.title: 22.4 Key Takeaways
items.text:
1. NUMA = local memory fast, remote memory slow; scheduler must be NUMA-aware
  2. First-touch = page allocated on node where first accessed
  3. Clock Algorithm = circular + ref bit; ref=1 → reset to 0, advance; ref=0 → replace
  4. Enhanced Clock = 4 classes by (ref, dirty); (0,0) evicted first (no write-back)
  5. Linux = uses enhanced clock variant

items.title: 22.5 Exam-Relevant MCQ Patterns
items.text:
• Q100: NUMA — local memory on CPU's local bus, lower latency than remote across interconnect
  • Q93: Clock — ref=1 → reset to 0, advance hand; ref=0 → replace
  • Q94: Enhanced Clock — (0,0) highest priority candidate for replacement
